title: tabularium sidecar
$comment: Contract FR-051, FR-052, FR-053, FR-057. Written as <archived-filename>.tabularium.json beside the archived file, on every successful filing — it is a trace of the processing, not an error log. JSON rather than YAML because it is machine-written and machine-read, never hand-edited. A file that fails to parse, carries an unknown `version`, or whose `source_digest` does not match the file it sits beside is treated as ABSENT: the anomaly is logged to stderr and the document is reprocessed from the start (FR-053). The bytes always win over the sidecar.

version.description: Sidecar schema version. A value this build does not know means the sidecar is treated as absent.

source.description: The path the document was filed from (FR-051).

source_digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source bytes. On re-run this is compared against the accompanying file; a mismatch means the sidecar belongs to something else and is treated as absent (FR-053).

metadata.description: The validated, normalised metadata, in the same shape as output.schema.json#/properties/metadata.

rule.description: Name of the rule that decided the destination (FR-037).

truncation.$comment: FR-008, FR-051 — recorded so the fact survives the run that discovered it.

archive.$comment: The state of the external hand-off (FR-051). This is what makes FR-052 possible: attempted=true with success=false is the signal to replay only the hand-off on the next run, and success=true means there is nothing left to do (exit 0).

exit_code.description: The external command's own exit code (FR-059).

output.description: Combined stdout and stderr, verbatim, truncated to 8 KiB (FR-057). Never parsed for an identifier: the archiver is a black box, and this trace is for a human to read.

error.description: Why the step failed when it failed before producing an exit code — binary not found (FR-060), timeout (FR-056).
